title: Using Speech-to-Text in a Document
subtitle: Student Guide
purpose: Help students use speech-to-text to draft ideas into a document before reviewing and editing their work.

subsections.title: What is it?
paragraphs: Speech-to-text lets you speak your ideas out loud and have them typed automatically into a document.
It can be useful when you want to get ideas down quickly, reduce typing fatigue, or focus on your thoughts before editing your writing.
subsections.imagePlaceholder: Document editor with the speech-to-text button highlighted
subsections.imageDescription: A document editor open on a blank page with the speech-to-text or microphone button highlighted.

subsections.title: What you need
bullets: A device with a document editor installed or available online
Internet access if the tool requires it

subsections.title: Before you begin
paragraphs: Check that your microphone is connected and working. Close other apps that may be using your microphone.
subsections.tip: Using headphones with a microphone can improve accuracy and reduce background noise.

subsections.title: Open your document editor
steps: Open your preferred document editor on your device.
Open a blank document or the document you want to work on.
subsections.tip: Have your topic, task instructions, or notes nearby before you start dictating.
subsections.imageDescription: The document editor start screen showing the option to open a blank document.

subsections.title: Start speech-to-text
steps: Find the speech-to-text, microphone, or dictate button.
Select the button to start listening.
subsections.imageDescription: The document toolbar with the speech-to-text or microphone button highlighted.

subsections.title: Speak your ideas
steps: Say punctuation such as comma, full stop, question mark, or new paragraph when needed.
subsections.tip: Dictation works best as a drafting tool. You can edit the wording afterwards.
subsections.imagePlaceholder: Dictated text appearing in the document
subsections.imageDescription: A document showing text appearing on the page after the student speaks.

subsections.title: Stop and review
steps: Select the speech-to-text button again to stop listening.
Read through the text and correct any errors.
Save your document in the required location.
subsections.imageDescription: A document editor showing options to save the file name and location.

helpfulTips.whyItHelps: Helps the tool recognise your words more accurately.
Reduces background noise and transcription errors.
Helps you correct words, punctuation and sentence flow.

troubleshooting.whatToTry: Check your internet connection, app version, and whether the feature is available in your account.
Check microphone access and make sure the correct microphone is selected.
Speak a little slower, reduce background noise, and review the text afterwards.

faqs.question: Do I need to type at all?
faqs.answer: You can use speech-to-text for drafting, but you should still review and edit your work.

faqs.question: Can I use speech-to-text for assignments?
faqs.answer: Yes. Speech-to-text can help you draft notes, paragraphs or ideas before editing.

faqs.question: Does speech-to-text work for long documents?
faqs.answer: Yes, although working in shorter sections often makes reviewing and editing easier.
